enonce_markdown: Element X has atomic number 16. (X is not its usual symbol.) In which group and period of the periodic table is it found?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Write the electronic configuration from the atomic number. The number of electrons in the outer shell gives the group; the number of occupied shells gives the period.

### Solution

Atomic number 16 means 16 electrons: configuration **2, 8, 6**.

- 6 electrons in the outer shell: **Group VI**.
- 3 occupied shells: **Period 3**.

**Answer: C.** Option A swaps the two numbers (group 3, period 6); B has only two shells (that is oxygen); D would need a full outer shell of 8.

enonce_markdown:
(i) Write the electronic configuration of (a) chlorine (atomic number 17) and (b) calcium (atomic number 20).

(ii) State the group and the period of each of these two elements.

(iii) Why is chlorine placed in Group VII? *[5 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Fill the shells in the order 2, 8, 8, 2... Then group = number of outer electrons and period = number of occupied shells.

### Solution

(i) (a) Chlorine, 17 electrons: **2, 8, 7**. (b) Calcium, 20 electrons: **2, 8, 8, 2**.

(ii) Chlorine: 7 outer electrons and 3 shells, so **Group VII, Period 3**. Calcium: 2 outer electrons and 4 shells, so **Group II, Period 4**.

(iii) Chlorine atoms have **seven electrons in the outer shell**, like the other elements of that vertical column (fluorine, bromine, iodine), so they have similar chemical properties and belong to Group VII.

enonce_markdown: Which statement about the Group I metals lithium, sodium and potassium is correct?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Going down a group, the atoms have more electron shells, so the outer electron is further from the nucleus and held less strongly. Use this to predict how easily a metal loses its outer electron.

### Solution

Down Group I the atoms get larger, the single outer electron is further from the nucleus and is **lost more easily**, so reactivity **increases** from lithium to potassium. **Answer: B.**

- A is wrong: more shells make the metals more reactive, not less.
- C is wrong: having the same number of outer electrons gives similar properties, but not identical reactivity.
- D is wrong: the number of outer electrons is 1 for every Group I metal.

choix.texte: Reactivity decreases down the group because the atoms have more electron shells.
Reactivity increases down the group because the outer electron is lost more easily.
All three react equally fast because each has one electron in its outer shell.
Reactivity increases down the group because the number of outer electrons increases.

enonce_markdown: Reactivity of the Group VII elements decreases in the order chlorine > bromine > iodine. A more reactive halogen displaces a less reactive halogen from a solution of its halide. In which one of the following mixtures will a reaction take place?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

A halogen can only displace another halogen that is BELOW it in Group VII, because it is more reactive. Compare the position of the added halogen with that of the halide ion already in solution.

### Solution

Chlorine is above iodine in Group VII, so it is more reactive and displaces iodine from potassium iodide: $\mathrm{Cl_{2} + 2KI \rightarrow  2KCl + I_{2}}$. The colourless solution turns brown as iodine forms. **Answer: D.**

- A: iodine is less reactive than chlorine, so no reaction.
- B: bromine is less reactive than chlorine, so no reaction.
- C: iodine is less reactive than bromine, so no reaction.

choix.texte: Iodine solution added to potassium chloride solution
Bromine water added to potassium chloride solution
Iodine solution added to potassium bromide solution
Chlorine water added to potassium iodide solution

enonce_markdown:
An element Y has three occupied electron shells and two electrons in its outer shell.

(a) What is the atomic number of Y?

(b) Name Y and state its group and period.

(c) Name the element Z that lies directly below Y in the same group, in Period 4, and write its electronic configuration.

(d) Which is more reactive, Y or Z? Give a reason. *[6 marks]*
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Build the electronic configuration shell by shell: atomic number = total number of electrons. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer electrons and show a regular trend in reactivity down the group.

### Solution

(a) Configuration 2, 8, 2, so the atomic number is $2 + 8 + 2 = 12$.

(b) **Magnesium** (Mg); 2 outer electrons give **Group II**; 3 shells give **Period 3**.

(c) The element below magnesium in Group II is **calcium** (Ca, atomic number 20), with configuration **2, 8, 8, 2**.

(d) **Calcium** is more reactive. Its outer electrons are in the fourth shell, further from the nucleus, so they are lost more easily than those of magnesium (reactivity of metals increases down a group).

enonce_markdown:
The table gives the electronic configurations of five elements P, Q, R, S and T (the letters are not the usual symbols).

| Element | P | Q | R | S | T |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Electronic configuration | 2, 1 | 2, 8, 1 | 2, 8, 7 | 2, 8, 8 | 2, 8, 8, 1 |

Which one of the following statements is correct?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Read each configuration: outer electrons give the group, number of shells gives the period. Then test every statement against these two rules and against the trend in reactivity down Group I.

### Solution

P is lithium-like (Group I, Period 2), Q (Group I, Period 3), R (Group VII, Period 3), S (Group 0, Period 3) and T (Group I, Period 4).

- A is **correct**: S (2, 8, 8) has a full outer shell, so it is a noble gas and its atoms do not readily form bonds.
- B is wrong: Q and R both have three shells, so they are in the same PERIOD (Period 3), but Q is in Group I and R in Group VII.
- C is wrong: P and T both have one outer electron, so they are in the same GROUP, but P has 2 shells and T has 4, so they are in different periods.
- D is wrong: T is in the same group as P and is below it, so T is MORE reactive because its outer electron is further from the nucleus.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: S has a full outer shell, so its atoms are unreactive.
Q and R are in the same group because both have three shells.
P and T are in the same period because both have one outer electron.
T is less reactive than P because it has more electron shells.
